spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Global record maximality becomes local factorization rigidity by constructing a smaller competitor that swaps the largest prime for one more power of a chosen smaller prime.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The SA definition implies consecutive superabundant numbers differ by at most a factor of two, since sigma(2n)/(2n)>sigma(n)/n. The unit also quotes a three-value relation between exponents at primes q<r. Its main proof assumes k_q is too small, forms m=nq^(k+1)/p with q^(k+1)<p, and uses multiplicativity plus SA maximality to obtain the contradictory inequality p<q^(k+1).
directed.conceptual_reading: A record property over all smaller integers is probed through a carefully chosen one-coordinate perturbation. The resulting exchange inequality forces every prime exponent to be large enough relative to the largest prime.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The competitor m=nq^(k+1)/p is the bridge between order in the integers and geometry of the exponent vector; multiplicativity reduces the global comparison to the changed prime-power factors.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument depends on m being an integer smaller than n and on strict SA record maximality. It establishes a lower bound on exponents, not their exact values; the quoted three-value proposition is not proved in this span.
directed.uncertainty: The competitor mechanism and exponent bound are clear; the dense extracted divisor-sum ratio should be verified before exact symbolic reuse.

supported: The consecutive-SA factor-two proof and the exact competitor m=nq^(k+1)/p are correctly reported.
The candidate correctly explains that multiplicativity reduces the global SA comparison to the altered prime-power factors and yields the contradiction p<q^(k+1).
It correctly limits the conclusion to a lower exponent bound and notes that the three-value proposition is only quoted.
inference: Viewing the competitor as a probe of exponent-vector geometry is a useful source-grounded interpretation.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous claim that the construction swaps p for 'one more power' of q is imprecise: multiplying n by q^(k+1)/p raises the existing q-exponent from k to 2k+1, rather than adding only one q factor.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The one-coordinate-perturbation language is useful only after the magnitude of that coordinate change is stated correctly.
context_or_ocr_risk: The dense divisor-sum ratio is legible enough to certify the mechanism, though exact symbolic reuse still warrants rendering.
missed_mechanism: The competitor is smaller specifically because q^(k+1)<p, while retaining divisibility because q^k and p already divide n.
revision_instructions: Replace 'one more power' with an exact description: remove the largest-prime factor p and multiply by q^(k+1), so the q-exponent changes from k to 2k+1; retain the smaller-competitor condition q^(k+1)<p.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Chebyshev oscillation produces infinitely many CA numbers with p(N) greater than log N, whereas every XA number has p(n) less than log n, so infinitely many CA numbers cannot be XA.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This separates one infinite CA subsequence only; it does not characterize all of CA minus XA or decide RH.

The assigned dossier identifies the underlying contrast as infinitely many CA with p(N)>log N versus the XA bound p(n)<log n.
directed.conceptual_reading: Class noncontainment is certified by finding a structural invariant with disjoint inequalities, not by enumerating examples. Recurrent occupation of one side by CA forces an infinite separation from XA.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The normalized largest-prime coordinate p(n)/log n is the separating statistic that makes two differently defined record classes comparable.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The decisive prior theorems and their proofs are not present in this span. The result isolates an infinite subset of CA outside XA but does not characterize CA minus XA, exclude infinite overlap, or decide RH.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the stated theorem and dossier-linked mechanism; the narrow artifact alone does not independently verify the antecedent prime-scale results.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The proved conditional monotonicity and the computed one-step exponent, spacing, ratio, and composition patterns suggest a coordinated local rigidity program for consecutive XA numbers.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Most parents here are finite computations with fixed cutoffs and external-list dependence; they are hypothesis generators, not universal evidence.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Finite XA data suggest a locally rigid exponent-vector path: adjacent prime-power layers stay in narrow bands and consecutive records change each exponent by at most one.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using XA terms through the 13770th element below C1, the source reports inequalities relating q^(k_q), neighboring r^(k_r), p, and log n; places the largest exponent-two prime between sqrt(p) and sqrt(2p); observes coordinate changes in {-1,0,1} for consecutive XA terms; and observes nondecreasing largest prime and divisor count. Examples show that the divisor-count observation does not make XA highly composite and that analogous monotonicities fail for SA.
directed.conceptual_reading: The observations treat factorizations as trajectories in exponent space and propose bounded local moves rather than isolated numerical coincidences. The counterexamples are important controls separating XA rigidity from stronger or neighboring extremal notions.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Prime-power blocks and primorial factorizations expose the exponent vector compactly; consecutive-XA comparison turns a static factorization into a discrete transition rule.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Every positive claim is empirical below the stated C1 cutoff and depends on an external SA list. None should be promoted to a theorem, and the supplied counterexamples explicitly block two tempting implications.
directed.uncertainty: The finite-status qualifiers and qualitative patterns are clear; exact prime-power inequalities should retain verified typeset notation.
